title: Disney+ Strikes Landmark Content Deal With U.K.’s Channel 4 That Streamer Says Is Among Its ‘Most Significant’ Globally
description: Disney+ has made what it claims is one of the “most significant’ content arrangements with broadcasters around the world to bring local content to
body:
Disney+ has made what it claims is one of the “most significant’ content arrangements with broadcasters around the world to bring local content to its platform, striking a landmark deal with U.K. network Channel 4. 

	The first-of-its-kind deal will see the Channel 4 service launch on Disney+ in the U.K. and Ireland in early 2027, with multiple Channel 4 shows made available on-demand each year on Disney+ at the same time as their release via Channel 4.  These shows include the drama “Maya” featuring Bella Ramsey, comedy “Stepping Up” featuring Denise Welch and reality format “Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins,” alongside – Channel 4’s main TV channel and additional on-demand content.
	

	The deal is one of around ten similar content deals that Disney has signed with international broadcasters, since it broke new ground last year following a deal with Brit streamer ITVX to share select content. That groundbreaking deal came just weeks after Netflix unveiled a landmark agreement in France to give its subscribers access to TF1 channels via the streamer.

	News of the collaboration with Channel 4 was described as “one of the most significant that Disney+ has agreed globally to bring high-quality, local content to customers in markets around the world,” according to Disney, something it said would enhance “Channel 4’s reach” and bring “more choice to Disney+ customers.”

	As per the deal, Disney+ customers will be able to watch Channel 4’s linear HD channel, plus hundreds of hours of its scripted and unscripted content through its on-demand catalogue, for no additional cost. The on-demand offering will feature a range of Channel 4 shows available day and dat’ on Disney+ – with Disney+ customers gaining access to multiple new Channel 4 shows each year as part of their existing subscription. Channel 4 will be available via a Channel 4-branded section.
	

	“We’re thrilled to be working with Disney+ to give audiences even more ways to discover and enjoy Channel 4’s brilliant shows,” said Priya Dogra, Channel 4 chief executive. “Channel 4 is home to some of the UK and Ireland’s most talked about and trusted programming, and this new service will help those shows reach viewers in new places. This exciting step shows how collaboration between broadcasters and streamers can create more choice and value for audiences.”

	Added Adam Smith, chairman direct-to-consumer, Disney Entertainment: “Local broadcaster partnerships are very important as we build our content libraries and serve fans around the world. Channel 4 has created shows with strong appeal to audiences in the UK and Ireland, and we’re excited to bring some of those favorites to Disney+. This agreement is the latest example of our global strategy, pairing high-quality local programming and cultural relevance with a complementary audience and more personalized streaming experience on Disney+.”

schema.headline: Disney+ Strikes Landmark Content Deal With U.K.’s Channel 4 That Streamer Says Is Among Its ‘Most Significant’ Globally

title: Macklemore Calls for Unity During First ‘Free Palestine’ Show: ‘Those Two Words Are So Threatening to Some People’
description: Macklemore dedicated his “Free Palestine” tour date to “love and liberation” as he kicked off the three-show trek in Dublin, Ireland, just over a m
body:
Macklemore dedicated his “Free Palestine” tour date to “love and liberation” as he kicked off the three-show trek in Dublin, Ireland, just over a month after he was dropped as an opener for Ed Sheeran following a political speech on stage.

	After bringing out Hozier and Kneecap as surprise guests, Macklemore took a moment to share what the evening meant to him in the wake of the controversy. “Six weeks ago, it was two words. Two words is all that it took. Two words that are rooted in love and liberation,” he said. “Not against anybody, not divisive. Not a call for hatred. But a call to recognize our shared humanity. Free Palestine. I said free Palestine! The same thing that I want for all of us, freedom, dignity, the right to exist without fear. Being able to raise our children in the homes that we grew up in, not having to prove our humanity to the rest of the world.
	

	“And yet,” he continued, “those words, those two words, right, those two words are so threatening to some people. They would rather silence those two words than confront what they actually mean. Because freedom that requires another person’s oppression is not freedom at all. I said freedom that requires another person’s oppression is not freedom at all. And while the world debates those words, we see the videos, we see the footage, we see parents pulling their children out of the rubble. Families erased. Devastation beyond our imagination. And somehow, those words have become more controversial than the suffering that made them necessary. That’s why we are here tonight. That is why we are here, because throughout history, music has given people a place to resist, to come together as a collective, to share our grief, to share our stories, to move from the heart, to mobilize people with the frequency of love. The heartbeat in our drum that makes us feel alive, that makes us feel connected.”
	

Macklemore kicks off his “Free Palestine” tour with a call for unity just over a month after being dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour over his political remarks onstage:“Six weeks ago, it was two words. Two words is all that it took. Two words that are rooted in love and… pic.twitter.com/xRomzGlMek— Variety (@Variety) October 26, 2026


	The Dublin concert is the first of a three-show stint that will see the “Thrift Shop” rapper also perform in Paris and London alongside special guests, with all proceeds going to charities supporting Palestine. Macklemore also donated his $1 million salary from Sheeran’s tour to the cause.

	On Sept. 14, Macklemore was dropped from the remainder of Sheeran’s U.S. “Loop” tour after he said “free Palestine” on stage and gave political speeches over two concerts at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sept. 4 and 5. “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: ‘Free Palestine.’ I said, ‘Free Palestine!’” Macklemore said at the Sept. 4 show. “I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them.” 

	The speech went viral, sparking backlash from pop star Pink and a petition from the Israeli American Council calling for Macklemore to be removed from Sheeran’s tour. “This was an Ed Sheeran concert — not a political rally, not a protest and not an activist event,” they said. “The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda.”

	On Sept. 5, he once again said “free Palestine” but also added that his declaration was “in no way a criticism” of Jewish people. A week later, he was dropped from the tour. At the time, Messina Touring Group — the promoter behind Sheeran’s U.S. tour — said they had been “notified by venues” that “they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.”

	In solidarity with Macklemore, Sheeran’s other opening acts — including Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe — as well as most of his backing band dropped out of the tour.

	Macklemore then claimed that Robert Kraft, owner of the Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts, refused to let him play at the venue and urged other stadium owners to do the same. Kraft responded by announcing that both he and Sheeran would be donating $2 million to “aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis.” Sheeran also posted a lengthy statement saying that the decision to drop Macklemore was the promoter’s, not his, and explaining why he chooses not to speak out on political issues, which generated further backlash against him.
	

	“Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care. Nor does it mean I don’t support causes in my own, personal way,” Sheeran wrote. “There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics — my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds. Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change.”

	But at his first show since Macklemore was dropped, on Sept. 19 in Philadelphia, Sheeran changed his tune and did speak up about the Israel-Gaza war. “What happened in Israel and at the Nova Music Festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable, and disproportionate,” he said. “Our hearts can be broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians’ lives, children’s lives and the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”

	Macklemore, who performed a one-off show on October 22 at Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre, continues his “Free Palestine” tour in Paris on Thursday and in London on Friday.

schema.headline: Macklemore Calls for Unity During First ‘Free Palestine’ Show: ‘Those Two Words Are So Threatening to Some People’

title: ‘The Odyssey’ VFX House DNEG Co-Finances Francesco Lucente’s Fantasy Adventure ‘Sinbad,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: DNEG, the visual effects house on Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” has come aboard Francesco Lucente’s fantasy adventure “Sinbad” as co-financier
body:
DNEG, the visual effects house on Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” has come aboard Francesco Lucente’s fantasy adventure “Sinbad” as co-financier and producer, with Hong Kong-based Cappu Films handling sales in a wide spread of territories.

	The deal was unveiled ahead of the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market. Lucente’s fresh screen version of the classic sailor tale is due to begin pre-production in early 2027 and to deliver in March 2029. 
	

	Cappu first showed the project to buyers at the Busan market, and sales conversations are ongoing as casting and the wider package take shape.

	“‘Sinbad’ is a story that has captured imaginations for generations, and our ambition is to bring it to life on a scale and with a sense of wonder that audiences have never experienced before,” said Lucente, who wrote the script and will direct. “We’re creating a breathtaking world of adventure, extraordinary creatures, ancient mysteries and unforgettable characters, while keeping the heart of the story deeply human. Having DNEG’s extraordinary creative talent behind us, together with Cappu Films’ international reach and commitment to the project, gives us an incredible foundation to realize that vision. We want ‘Sinbad’ to be more than a spectacular cinematic experience – we want it to be the kind of adventure that stays with audiences long after they leave the theater.”

	The sales company’s rights cover parts of Asia, Europe, the CIS, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East and Africa, along with some Pacific island markets. China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, German-speaking Europe, Spain, Portugal, Turkey and Eastern Europe are all on the list.
	

	The film reunites Cappu with Lucente after “Starbright.” Janice Woo of Cappu Films said that following their work together on that film, the company was excited to team with the director on a project of this scale. “DNEG’s involvement is particularly compelling for a fantasy adventure such as ‘Sinbad.’ We introduced the project to buyers in Busan and look forward to developing those conversations as the package comes together,” Woo said.

	DNEG’s teams have won eight Oscars for visual effects, and the company’s credits include “Inception,” “Interstellar,” “Blade Runner 2049,” “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two.”

	Lucente’s fantasy feature “Starbright” counts Ted Levine, John Rhys-Davies and Diego Boneta among its cast. He also directed the drama “Badland.” Cappu is separately handling international sales on “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller starring Joseph Mazzello and set at Los Angeles’ Cecil Hotel.

	Cappu partners with independent filmmakers on both arthouse and commercial titles. Its catalog takes in horror, action, fantasy and arthouse fare, alongside library titles from Hong Kong’s Golden Era and TV series.

schema.headline: ‘The Odyssey’ VFX House DNEG Co-Finances Francesco Lucente’s Fantasy Adventure ‘Sinbad,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: India’s Oscar Entry ‘Gondhal’ Unveils Global Trailer (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Gondhal,” the Marathi-language thriller India has put forward for the international feature Oscar at the 99th Academy Awards, has launched its glo
body:
“Gondhal,” the Marathi-language thriller India has put forward for the international feature Oscar at the 99th Academy Awards, has launched its global trailer as its awards push moves into a new phase.

	The film is the first feature from writer-director Santosh Davakhar. It was chosen from a field of 33 films in contention for India’s submission.

	The story plays out over a single night in rural Maharashtra, during a Gondhal, a folk ritual in which devotion is expressed through song, dance and theatrical storytelling. Ishita Deshmukh plays Suman, a young wife stuck in a suffocating marriage. She tries to take back control by playing on the fixation her lover Sarjerao (Nishad Bhoir) has developed for her. As her desires run up against codes of honor and custom, the night ends in tragedy.
	

	Kishor Kadam, Yogesh Sohoni and Anuj Prabhu also star. Amalendu Chaudhary shot the film, which opens with an unbroken take lasting 25 minutes. Legendary composer Ilaiyaraaja wrote the music and background score. 

	“Global perceptions of Indian cinema are often shaped by narratives of poverty and caste conflict – important realities, but not the complete expression of India,” said Davakhar. “India is also a civilization of extraordinary cultural wealth, sustained by traditions, music, and collective memory. I created this film to bring one such powerful tradition to the global screen through a culturally authentic and universal cinematic language.”

	Davakhar won the Silver Peacock for best director at the 56th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Jury members at the festival called the film “like a Shakespearean fable set in a real world.”
	

	Davakhar produced the film with Diksha Davakhar, his co-founder at production banner Davakhar Films. The company backs regional stories and aims for top-tier craft in camera work, sound, music and acting.

title: ‘Call of Duty’ Movie Will Be About the ‘Cost of War and Having to Be a Warrior,’ Says Director: ‘These Are Not Comic Books or Cartoon Characters’
description: Paramount Pictures’ upcoming “Call of Duty” movie, based on the massively popular video game franchise, is definitely not going to feel like a comi
body:
Paramount Pictures’ upcoming “Call of Duty” movie, based on the massively popular video game franchise, is definitely not going to feel like a comic book tentpole or make soldiers out to be superheroes, director Peter Berg recently told ComicBook. The “Friday Night Lights” and “Lone Survivor” director is helming the video game adaptation from a script by Taylor Sheridan. The movie will draw inspiration from the “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare” games.
	

	“If you really look at the missions and the storylines and the characters like Captain Price, Soap, Ghost and Alex, these are complicated humans. These are not, and no disrespect, cartoon characters or comic books. These are very nuanced storylines; there’s a real soul to the ‘Modern Warfare’ universe. Yes, there’s violence and hardware and equipment and killing. But underneath it, I think the game, and the creators of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who’s, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry.”


	Beginning with “Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare” in 2007, the “Modern Warfare” storyline marked the first “Call of Duty” video game to break from the franchise’s original World War II setting. Paramount has yet to reveal any plot details for its upcoming film adaptation, nor has any casting information been made available.

	Berg noted at CinemaCon earlier this year that “Taylor and I are both deeply connected to the special ops community” before a sizzle reel highlighted the video game franchise’s continued successes, including 1 billion players and a lifetime revenue of $35 billion.
	

	Paramount announced its “Call of Duty” movie in September 2025. Sources said at the time that while the pact is focused on making one “Call of Duty” movie, the deal included the potential for Paramount to expand the “Call of Duty” universe across film and TV. The movie is currently on Paramount’s release schedule for June 30, 2028.

schema.headline: ‘Call of Duty’ Movie Will Be About the ‘Cost of War and Having to Be a Warrior,’ Says Director: ‘These Are Not Comic Books or Cartoon Characters’

title: Eric Bauza’s ‘Looney Tunes’ Legacy: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Producer Says Voice Actor Behind Bugs Bunny and More Had a ‘Deep Love of the Craft’
description: Chris DeFaria, the former president of animation and innovative technology at Warner Bros. and producer of “Coyote vs. Acme,” shared his thoughts o
body:
Chris DeFaria, the former president of animation and innovative technology at Warner Bros. and producer of “Coyote vs. Acme,” shared his thoughts on the sudden death of Eric Bauza, the voice of many “Looney Tunes” characters. 

	I’m heartbroken to share that my friend and colleague Eric Bauza passed away last night. The world lost a great voice.

	Eric carried the legacy of Looney Tunes with a devotion few bring to their work. He voiced Daffy Duck, Bugs Bunny, Porky Pig, Marvin the Martian, and so many more. And he never treated them as a job. To him, they were icons who deserved to be honored, protected, and kept alive for new generations. He championed these characters tirelessly in every room he walked into.
	

	Eric never forgot whose shoulders he stood on either. He had enormous reverence for Mel Blanc, the master who gave these characters their original voices, and he used to say he was only borrowing Mel’s Cadillac, and that he promised to return the keys when he was done. That was Eric.

	A man handed one of the great legacies in animation, who treated it as a trust rather than a trophy. He drove it with love and cared with a little bit of mischief, and he left it in better shape than when he found it. 

	After Mel’s passing in 1989, the voices he carried by himself were divided among many talented performers.

	Then Eric came along. 

	He started by trying a few of the voices, and in what felt like no time at all, he was doing nearly all of them. It’s a feat that few, if any, had pulled off since Mel himself. 

	But what Eric achieved went far beyond impressions. Learning the sound of a character is hard enough. Eric did something deeper. 
	

	He learned to be them, to think like Bugs, to scheme like Daffy, to stutter and squirm like Porky. That’s why they never sounded like imitations when he performed them. They sounded alive.

	What made it more remarkable was that his talent was largely his own. He was self-taught, and he built that astonishing range through curiosity, relentless practice, and a deep love of the craft. You could hear that love in every line. I was lucky enough to share time with Eric at Warner Brothers, and luckier still to have worked alongside him most recently on “Coyote vs Acme.”

	Eric had a devilish wit, and was never more alive than when he stepped into those characters with a mischievous spark that made them feel new while honoring everyone who came before them.

	And yes, Eric was always late. I like to think that somewhere right now, Bugs, in fact, is tapping his foot and checking his watch, and Eric is strolling in with a grin, a perfect excuse in a line so funny that all is forgiven within seconds. 

	He was worth the wait every single time.

	Thank you, Eric, for the laughter, the artistry, the joy you gave us all. I know you promised to return Mel’s keys when you’re done. Take your time. You always did.

	— As told to Jazz Tangcay

schema.headline: Eric Bauza’s ‘Looney Tunes’ Legacy: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Producer Says Voice Actor Behind Bugs Bunny and More Had a ‘Deep Love of the Craft’

title: Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie to Star in Christina Kallas’ Thriller ‘He Talks to Me’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie will star in “He Talks to Me,” a psychological thriller from director Christina Kallas and screenwriter Alejandro Ada
body:
Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie will star in “He Talks to Me,” a psychological thriller from director Christina Kallas and screenwriter Alejandro Adams, Variety can reveal exclusively. 

	Mike S. Ryan developed the project and will produce through his banner Greyshack Films. Derrick Tseng will also produce.

	According to an official logline, “He Talks to Me” follows “Melody (Gabor), a young single mother in rural Arkansas, who is followed home by local police officer Bryce Hagan (Langlie) for what begins as a casual interrogation and spirals into a harrowing test of survival, coercion and endurance.” Other cast members include Sayra Player, Adam David Thompson and Ryan Siegel. 
	

	Other projects from Kallas, a two-time Berlinale and Slamdance alumna, include “Paris is in Harlem” and “The Rainbow Experiment.” She is a former president of the Federation of Screenwriters in Europe and a member of the Actors Studio.

	Gabor recently wrapped production on Tony Goldwyn‘s “Hello Darkness” and can next be seen in a recurring role in Season 3 of “Daredevil: Born Again.” Her other recent film credits include David Michod’s “Christy,” “The Friend” with Bill Murray and Greyson Horst’s “Throuple.” On the small screen, she starred in Season 2 of the Paramount+ series “School Spirits” and had a breakout performance on Season 9 and Season 10 of “Shameless.”

	Arthur was last seen in Kent Jones’ 2025 drama “Late Fame,” which starred Willem Dafoe and Greta Lee. His upcoming credits include “Cut Your Teeth,” from director Samuel Goodwin and producer Aaron Moorhead, and” Trash Pandas,” from director Ana Brown and producer Peter Cambor.
	

	Gabor is repped by Anonymous Content, Buchwald, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman; Langlie by UTA; Adams by Range Media Partners; Thompson by CGF Talent; Player by Exclusive Artists Agency; and Siegel by Avenue B Talent.

schema.headline: Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie to Star in Christina Kallas’ Thriller ‘He Talks to Me’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Lionsgate Forms Joint Venture With Steven Paul, Movie Producer Who Has Had Trump’s Ear
description: Lionsgate and Steven Paul, an entrepreneur and film producer who has personally lobbied President Donald Trump on a federal tax incentive for Holly
body:
Lionsgate and Steven Paul, an entrepreneur and film producer who has personally lobbied President Donald Trump on a federal tax incentive for Hollywood, are forming a joint venture through which Paul’s SP Media will make a “significant” investment in new initiatives together with Lionsgate.

	The amount of Paul’s planned investment into the JV was not disclosed. A source familiar with the agreement said SP Media’s initial investment will be around $100 million, with the potential for a similar amount to be invested in the future.
	

	Under the agreement, SP Media also will produce independent feature films that Lionsgate will distribute. The relationship will be managed through the joint venture, which will be majority owned and controlled by Lionsgate. It’s understood that the joint venture’s investments will be into new businesses that expand Lionsgate’s content, including the continued diversification of 3 Arts Entertainment, Lionsgate’s talent management and production division, into new areas like sports and influencers.

	Paul, who serves as chairman, founder and CEO of Crystal Sky Pictures and SP Media Group, has shepherded several box-office successes in years past, including the Baby Geniuses franchise, “Ghost Rider” and “Ghost Rider 2: Spirit of Vengeance” starring Nicolas Cage, “Ghost in the Shell” starring Scarlett Johansson, and the Lionsgate-distributed “Rambo: Last Blood.”

	More recently, Paul has been working with actor Jon Voight to pitch Trump on a series of measures to help the U.S. entertainment industry, including a federal tax incentive for TV and film productions. At an Aug. 31 meeting at the White House, Paul cited his upcoming film about Richard Nixon’s early years — telling Trump the project would need to be produced overseas unless there is a viable U.S. tax incentive.
	

	The announcement of the JV between Lionsgate and SP Media comes after a report last week that Legendary Entertainment revived its bid to acquire Lionsgate.

	“Steven is a savvy and experienced entrepreneur who has a longstanding relationship with our studio, and I’m pleased to partner with him across multiple touchpoints of our business,” Lionsgate CEO Jon Feltheimer said in announcing the agreement. “He recognizes the unique and valuable assets that we have built and his investment will help drive the continued growth of these businesses.”

	Paul said in a statement: “Lionsgate is one of the most dynamic and entrepreneurial content studios in the media space today. I’m delighted to build on my longstanding relationship with Jon Feltheimer and the Lionsgate leadership team as we grow our businesses together in an industry environment filled with opportunity.”

	Paul’s SP Group of Companies has holdings in media, entertainment, talent representation, technology, hospitality, banking and real estate. The portfolio includes the Samuel Goldwyn Building in Century City; the Casa Marella Boutique Hotel in South Beach Miami; the JLTV television network; Atlas Comics (founded by Marvel Comics owner Martin Goodman); Avenue Six Studios in Van Nuys, California; Echo Bridge Distribution Co.; and Hanks Café in Century City.

	The deal was negotiated for Lionsgate by COO Brian Goldsmith, EVP and general counsel Bruce Tobey and senior VP of corporate development Suzy Felfeli and for SP Media by group president and COO Scott Karol. Moelis served as financial adviser to Lionsgate and Lazard served as financial adviser to SP Media. Law firm Paul Hastings repped SP Media on the deal.

schema.headline: Lionsgate Forms Joint Venture With Steven Paul, Movie Producer Who Has Had Trump’s Ear

title: Walter Koenig, Chekov on ‘Star Trek,’ Remembered by George Takei: ‘Keep Navigating a Steady Course’
description: Walter Koenig‘s “Star Trek” colleagues are remembering the actor who played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series, calling him “a loyal friend.
body:
Walter Koenig‘s “Star Trek” colleagues are remembering the actor who played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series, calling him “a loyal friend.” Koenig died Sunday in Los Angeles. His “Star Trek” co-star George Takei reminisced over Koenig serving as best man at his wedding.

	Takei, who played Lieutenant Hikaru Sulu, wrote on Instagram, “My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today.
	

	“Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades,” the post continued. “When Brad and I married in 2008, Walter stood beside us as our best man. Just last month, on Sept. 14, he turned 90, on the same day Brad and I celebrated our 18th wedding anniversary. I will always treasure that he and I shared that date. Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend. To the fans who loved him for so many years, thank you. He loved you too. Rest well, my dear friend. Keep navigating a steady course.”


	Adam Nimoy, Leonard Nimoy’s son, wrote, “So sad to hear about the loss of Walter Koenig. Such a nice guy and when we were on the convention circuit together a pleasure to hang out with. Here he is with Celeste Yarnall in ‘The Apple,’ one of my favorites of the oddball episodes. Farewell.”

So sad to hear about the loss of Walter Koenig. Such a nice guy and when we were on the convention circuit together a pleasure to hang out with. Here he is with Celeste Yarnall in “The Apple”, one of my favorites of the oddball episodes. Farewell. pic.twitter.com/NuUJvHgR3h— Adam Nimoy (@adam_nimoy) October 26, 2026


	Michael Okuda, a scenic artist and technical consultant on several “Star Trek” installments, recalled his interview for the Roddenberry archive, writing, “Mourning the passing of Star Trek legend Walter Koenig. He was 90. A couple of years ago, Walter gave us a nice interview for the Roddenberry Archive.”
	

	Koenig’s reps said in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece.

	“Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond ‘Star Trek,’ his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft. His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film ‘Mr. Fleischmann,’ for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards — a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft…

	“Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.”

schema.headline: Walter Koenig, Chekov on ‘Star Trek,’ Remembered by George Takei: ‘Keep Navigating a Steady Course’

title: Pasifika Entertainment Advancement Komiti Announces 2026 Writers Fellowship Class
description:
The Pasifika Entertainment Advancement Komiti has named the third cohort of its annual PEAK Writers Fellowship.

	This year’s cohort includes Kanan
body:
The Pasifika Entertainment Advancement Komiti has named the third cohort of its annual PEAK Writers Fellowship.

	This year’s cohort includes Kanani Koster, Erin Lau, Sean Oketani, Neil Tinkham and Pouariʻi Tanne. Supported by Netflix, the fellowship selects five up-and-coming writers whose work honors Pasifika (people of Pacific Islander descent) experiences, providing them with mentorship, professional development and networking opportunities as they continue to expand their professional television careers.
	

	Founded by PEAK co-founder, director, screenwriter and showrunner Dana Ledoux Miller and co-managed by program manager and screenwriter Bryson Chun, the fellowship serves as the only Hollywood writing program created by a Pasifika storyteller.

	“I’m so grateful that in this time of industry uncertainty, Netflix continues to invest in emerging writers,” Miller said. “Fellowships like this not only make it possible for our communities to steward our own stories from script to screen, they allow the five incredible writers in this year’s fellowship to challenge and upend expectations of who we are expected to be as artists.”

	Each fellow is paired with an experienced industry mentor who helps refine their scripts to be professionally presented. Also included in the fellowship are weekly panels and conversations with writers, showrunners, executives, representatives, actors and other industry professionals, offering insight on the entertainment industry.

	This year’s fellows will receive mentorship from Ryan Belenzon and Jeffrey Gelber (“Boulevard”); Aminta Goyel (“Pivoting”); Lauren Thompson (“Ghostwriter”); and Michelle Giannusa (“Ripple”).
	

	“We received a record number of applications this year, which shows how sorely this fellowship is needed,” said Averie Huffine, the interim executive director of PEAK. “But I think it’s also due to Netflix being synonymous with great programming, and the reputation of Dana and Bryson’s incredible mentorship.”

	See the list of fellows below.

	Kanani Koster — “Clinic Daze”



	

	



	A half-hour dramedy following the ragtag yet passionate staff of an underfunded abortion clinic hustling to provide compassionate care to their patients, all while navigating their own chaotic personal lives.

	Koster is a native Hawaiian writer and director. Her work uses raunchy blue comedy to hide a desire to make a difference in this world. Kanani is a 2024 American Film Institute directing alum, 2024 ‘Ohina Lab Fellow and ‘23 Punky Aloha Scholar for Kanaka ‘Ōiwi and Pasifika Creatives. Her work has been supported by the Tribeca Film Festival, Gotham’s Project Market, Visionary Justice Story Lab and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. Her shorts have played at AFI Fest, SeriesFest, Hawai’i International Film Festival, and the Smithsonian Museum.

	Erin Lau — “The Hālau”



	

	



	“The Hālau” is a one-hour family drama that follows 16-year-old Maile Johnson who, after her mother’s death, is forced to live with her estranged family on Oahu and enter the world of competitive hula dancing.

	The Native Hawaiian filmmaker explores empathy, redemption and legacy through her work. She has been supported by the Sundance Institute, Tribeca Studios, Film Independent, Ryan Murphy’s Half Initiative and more. Her work spans narrative, documentary and episodic storytelling and has been featured on the Criterion Channel, Netflix and PBS.Lu’s most recent directing credit was for Fox’s action-packed procedural “Rescue: HI-Surf.” She is also currently a fellow in the 2026 ImagineNATIVE Screenwriting Series Lab and the Sundance Institute | The Asian American Foundation (TAAF) Accelerator.

	Sean Oketani — “[Pair]adise”



	

	



	Two queer, hapa Hawaiian best friends decide to ditch their jobs as hotel servers and spend the day playing tourists in Waikīkī.

	Oketani is a Native Hawaiian writer, director and storyteller born and raised on the island of Oʻahu. He graduated from Chapman University’s Dodge College of Film and Media Arts with a BFA in television writing and production. He wrote and produced his undergraduate thesis, “Gay Church,” a short-form comedy pilot. He has worked across the programming, education, and outreach departments at the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival (HIFF). In 2025, he was selected as an ʻOhina Labs Writers Fellow and received the ʻOhina Judge’s Award for his short film script, currently in pre-production.
	

	His work often draws from the intersection of his identities and perspectives, navigating both lived and inherited experiences. He is passionate about crafting compelling narratives that explore the contradictions and overlaps of identity, culture and belonging. He is inspired by Indigenous and Pasifika cinema; queer art and literature; and the influence of digital culture, both on and offline.

	Neil Tinkham — “West Coast Chamorus”



	

	



	A straight-laced Chamoru father must confront his past as a gangbanger when he returns to Los Angeles with his son for medical treatment.

	Tinkham is a Chamoru filmmaker originally from Guam. His work reflects his island upbringing and the Chamoru diaspora community. His short movies have received funding from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the Pacific Islanders in Communications and the Guam Council for the Arts and Humanities Agency. His work has screened at film festivals and regional museums and received distribution. In 2018, Neil’s feature-length screenplay “Jungle” was optioned by New Zealand-based production company Popgun Filmmakers, and, in 2022, his screenplay “The Taotaomona” was selected for the Second Annual Indigenous List, compiled by the Sundance Institute, ImagineNative and The Black List. Other scripts Tinkham has written have placed in screenwriting labs and competitions, including the Ohina Filmmakers Lab and the Page International Screenwriting Awards.

	Pouariʻi Tanner — “The Assistant”



	

	



	When a Māori current affairs crew arrives in Hollywood to profile its Indigenous stars, they discover their promised access doesn’t exist and must navigate the assistants, gatekeepers and strange characters operating behind the scenes of the Indigenous entertainment industry.

	Tanner is a Cook Islands writer and producer based in Rarotonga. Her work draws on her experience across Indigenous film, television and media, using comedy and character-driven storytelling to explore the strange intersections between island communities and larger cultural institutions. She previously worked with the Sundance Institute’s Indigenous Program and created and produced the documentary series “Turtle Town” in the Cook Islands. She is currently developing three short films through Pasifika TV’s film masterclass, to be completed and released in 2027. Through her production company, Pacific Standard Time, she is developing original film and television projects from the Pacific.

            Bryson Tiller and Kristy Sarah were spotted getting cozy in South Africa ... months before we confirmed they're an item.
      
    
            Eyewitnesses tell TMZ they met Bryson backstage in July when he performed in South Africa alongside Swae Lee and Masego. When stopping by his green room to say hello, our sources tell us Bryson was sitting on a couch with Kristy.
      
    
            We're told the witness invited Kristy to join them for photos to avoid leaving her out ... but Bryson later asked to retake the pictures with just him, explaining they were trying to keep things private.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The eyewitness says they didn't think much of the interaction at the time, but they later spoke with Kristy and invited her to an afterparty ... where the two showed up and appeared "super cozy."
      
    
            The witness says they didn't recognize Kristy until seeing TMZ's recent coverage ... putting the pair together months before their connection caught their attention.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We broke the story ... after obtaining video of the two smooching over the weekend, sources familiar with the situation tell us they're not in a relationship, but are casually seeing each other and dating.
      
    
            It's unclear exactly when things sparked between the two, but this South Africa sighting suggests they may have been spending plenty of time together ... well before the recent buzz.

title: Convicted Murderer Jacob Allen Morley Escapes From Tennessee Prison
description:
Killer Jacob Allen Morley
                          Busts Out of Tennessee Prison ...
body:
Killer Jacob Allen Morley
                          Busts Out of Tennessee Prison ...
                          Allegedly Slipped Through Fence
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 26, 2026
                            2:38 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Jacob Allen Morley -- a convicted felon serving a life sentence for murder -- has allegedly broken out of prison and sparked a manhunt in Tennessee.
      
    
            The Tennessee Department of Correction announced the shocking news in a statement Monday ... stating he escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, TN, late Sunday night.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            TDOC states it has searched and cleared buildings and structures in the surrounding area ... and the Tennessee Highway Patrol is assisting with the investigation. So far, though, they have been unable to find him.
      

            According to TDOC ... a nearly 6-foot-tall Morley -- who weighs about 240 pounds -- allegedly escaped through a fence.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Tennessee Bureau of Investigations has added Morley to its Most Wanted list ... and a reward of up to $2,500 is available for info leading to his arrest.
      
    
            Residents are being asked to check home security and doorbell cameras and other surveillance systems ... while also being told not to approach him.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Morley was convicted of first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism last year in connection with the killing of Cody Birchfield. Birchfield was considered missing until authorities found him under Morley's house in 2022.
      
    
            This is the second embarrassing incident for the Tennessee Department of Correction in the last few weeks ... remember, this is the same department that unsuccessfully attempted to execute Christa Pike at the end of last month.

                          Irrestitible New Hairdo ...

            Jessica Simpson's apparently trying to figure out if brunettes can have as much fun as blondes ... because she's ditched her trademark locks for a more natural look
      
    
            The singer-songwriter was spotted hopping off a plane at LAX ... keeping a low profile in ripped jeans, a blue-and-red flannel and a T-shirt.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            On top of the toned-down ensemble, Jessica looked unrecognizable because she's gone from blonde to brunette ... flaunting her natural look as she headed down the escalator.
      

            It's pretty wild ... Jessica's been a card-carrying blonde bombshell for years -- so to see her embracing her natural hair color comes as quite the shock.
      
    
            Of course, Jessica's gone through several major life changes in recent years ... so a change in hair color really shouldn't be that notable.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Jessica and her husband of more than a decade, Eric Johnson, separated in early 2025 ... and she recently went public with her new boyfriend, Thomas Eisenhood. The pair were spotted hanging out at Albuquerque's Balloon Fiesta Park earlier this month... and Jessica was still sporting her long blonde locks.
      
    
            It may be different than what we're used to seeing ... but, hey, Jessica Simpson can pull off anything!

description:
'Love After Lockup'
                          Brittany Santiago & Hubby Marcelino's Divorce Dismi
body:
'Love After Lockup'
                          Brittany Santiago & Hubby Marcelino's Divorce Dismissed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 26, 2026
                            2:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            "Love After Lockup" star Brittany Santiago and her estranged husband Marcelino Santiago's divorce has been tossed out ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to docs obtained by TMZ ... the judge presiding over their case dismissed the divorce proceedings without prejudice because neither party moved the case forward.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            While this order means the two are still married ... theoretically Marcelino -- who filed for divorce -- could file papers again if he wanted to.
      

            We reported earlier ... Brittany seemed unbothered by Marcelino's divorce filing as she posted family photos of her kids in July.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Marcelino had initially filed for divorce in June ... calling the former couple "incompatible" as spouses at the time.
      
    
            Brittany -- who has reportedly faced criminal charges of conspiracy to commit robbery, attempted murder, battery, and kidnapping -- met Marcelino while she was serving time in prison.
